LEARNING PATH LESSON · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

Bus — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson rides the toddler’s own experience: the bus they have sat on, the song they half-know, and the doors that open and shut — naming each part as it happens.

What is this?

A bus is a big long vehicle that carries lots of people and goes beep beep — usually the machine a two-year-old has physically ridden.

What does it mean?

The bus is vocabulary attached to memory: the bumpy seat, the tall windows, the beep of the doors. Experience-backed words stick faster than any picture alone.

What does the child need to know?

The bus song about the wheels going round is the teaching tool built into this card — every verse is a body part or a bus part, sung while pointing at both.

Why this matters

Buses run on schedules and streets, so sightings are daily and the song is everywhere. The word rehearses itself at every window.

What it teaches

Song-and-gesture pairing, part-naming (wheels, doors, windows), and the first feel of public transport as a normal, nameable part of life.

Words to learn

busbeepwheelsdoorsridepeople

Say this to your child

“"A bus! Beep beep! The bus is big and long. Can you roll your wheels — round and round? The bus carries lots of people, and the doors go open and shut."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and say bus, then beep beep — two cheerful toots with your palm as the horn.
  2. Sing the bus’s own song while your finger taps the wheels on the card, then roll your hands round and round together.
  3. Hunt buses in books and toy baskets, then take up a window post and wait for a real one to rumble past.
  4. When your toddler answers with a beep, a wheel-roll or the first da of the song, join in exactly where they are and carry the verse.
  5. Give the bus its weekly job: if a real route runs nearby, stand at the stop once this week and watch the doors open and shut in person.

Look closer at the picture

Two words to find on this card: the label Bus and the sound words Beep beep. Point at each one, then ask where the wheels sit on the picture.

Ask your child

"Where is the bus?" "What does the bus say?" "Can you roll your hands like wheels?" "Who rides on the bus with us?"

What your child can say or do

"Bus!" with a palm-toot, or the round-and-round arm rolls started without any sound. Some toddlers will demand the song every bus sighting for months — let them; the verses are vocabulary.

Out in the real world

The real bus stop is this card’s graduation hall: watch a bus arrive, beep at it, name the wheels and the doors, then wave it off. If you ride one, the card comes too.

Try it together

Chair bus: line up kitchen chairs, take the driver’s seat, and sing the whole song with gestures — wheels, doors, mummies, daddies. Ticket-clipping with a pretend punch adds a job for small hands.

Understanding check

Ask what the bus says and what the wheels do. A beep plus round-and-round hands passes. At the next real sighting, a pointed finger and a toot means the card rode all the way home.

Parent tips

The song does the heavy lifting, so learn two verses well rather than five badly. Bus routes beat zoo trips for value: the same teaching opportunity drives past every day of the week.

Staying safe

At the stop, stand back from the kerb with a firm hand on your toddler — buses swing in close and their wheels hide small feet. On board, everyone sits or holds on from the first bump.

This lesson pairs with the Bus flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Vehicles & Sounds (Toddler 6).
